status: draft (sẽ FROZEN ở tuần 2 thành protocol v1.0)
study: Detecting and explaining client-side Web performance degradation with Explainable ML

controlled_testbed.role: fault injection with known cause for RQ3 (ground truth)

shopify_staging.role: case study before/after optimisation for RQ4

toolchain.browser: Google Chrome stable, headless (version recorded per row)

measurement_profile.network: slow-4G: request latency 562.5 ms, download 1474.56 Kbps, upload 675 Kbps
measurement_profile.note: devtools throttling so an injected N ms busy-wait really costs N ms; fresh Chrome per measurement; order shuffled with a fixed seed

feature_families.structural: what the page ships: requests, bytes by type, origins, DOM size
feature_families.runtime: what the browser does while loading: main-thread work, long tasks, render-blocking, unused code

cause_groups.main_thread_js: JavaScript execution blocking the main thread
cause_groups.third_party: third-party scripts and their network/CPU cost
cause_groups.dom_complexity: large DOM, style and layout work

faults.mechanism: after the load event, run `count` back-to-back tasks of `dose` ms busy-wait; dose 0 = baseline (same script, no work)
faults.expected_effect: TBT ≈ count × (dose − 50) ms; LCP roughly unchanged

validation.split: GroupKFold by site (RQ2): no site appears in both train and test
